comment: Setting notes: one or two plain sentences per user-visible setting, what it does and when to change it. Shown in the setting tooltip and by the MCP server and mimir. Keyed by setting key; packages/settings/js/notes.test.ts checks coverage, length and wording.

notes.brim_ears_detection_length: How much the outline is simplified before sharp corners are looked for, in mm. Raise it so small wiggles on curved parts don't each get an ear; 0 checks every corner.
notes.brim_ears_max_angle: Corners sharper than this angle get a brim ear. Raise it toward 180 to put ears on more corners; 0 puts ears nowhere.
notes.brim_ears_outer_only: Puts brim ears only on the outside of the part, not around holes. Turn it off when corners inside a hole also lift.
notes.brim_flow_ratio: Scales how much plastic the brim lines get, on top of the filament's flow ratio. Raise it a little if the brim prints thin and tears off the bed.
notes.brim_object_gap: Leaves a small gap between the brim and the part, in mm, so the brim snaps off cleanly. 0.1 to 0.2 mm is typical; too large and the brim stops holding the part down.
notes.brim_type: Adds flat rings around the first layer to hold the part to the bed. Auto adds one only where the part needs it; mouse ears put small discs under sharp corners only.
notes.brim_use_efc_outline: Lines the brim up with the first layer after elephant foot compensation shrinks it. Turn it on only when that compensation is large and the brim pulls away from the part.
notes.brim_width: How far the brim reaches out from the part, in mm. A wider brim holds better against warping and takes longer to print and peel off; 3 to 8 mm covers most parts.
notes.draft_shield: Builds the skirt up as a thin wall as tall as the print, which shields ABS and ASA from drafts on an open printer. Not needed in an enclosure.
notes.min_skirt_length: Adds skirt loops until at least this much filament has gone through the nozzle, in mm. Use it to prime the nozzle when the start G-code draws no purge line; 0 turns it off.
notes.raft_contact_distance: The vertical gap between the raft and the part, in mm. A larger gap makes the raft easier to remove and leaves a rougher underside.
notes.raft_expansion: How far every raft layer reaches past the part's footprint, in mm. A wider raft holds better and uses more filament.
notes.raft_first_layer_density: How densely the first raft or support layer is filled, in percent. Lower saves filament; higher sticks to the bed better.
notes.raft_first_layer_expansion: Makes the first raft or support layer wider than the rest, in mm, for better grip on the bed.
notes.raft_layers: Prints the part on this many layers of disposable raft. Use it for warping materials such as ABS or for parts with a small, rough footprint; it costs filament and leaves a rougher bottom.
notes.single_loop_draft_shield: Prints the skirt or draft shield as a single loop above the first layer to save filament. A one-loop shield is weaker and can crack or curl.
notes.skirt_distance: The gap between the skirt and the part or its brim, in mm.
notes.skirt_height: How many layers tall the skirt is. One layer is enough to prime the nozzle; more layers start to act as a draft shield.
notes.skirt_loops: Number of loops drawn around the parts before the print starts, which primes the nozzle and shows the first layer is level. 0 turns the skirt off.
notes.skirt_speed: Print speed for the skirt, in mm/s. 0 uses the first layer speed.
notes.skirt_start_angle: Where the skirt starts, as an angle around the parts' center: 0 is the right side and positive angles turn counterclockwise.
notes.skirt_type: Combined draws one skirt around all the parts; per object draws one around each part, which is useful when printing objects one at a time.
notes.support_ironing: Irons the top of the support interface flat, which gives a smoother underside on the part above. The interface prints solid when this is on.
notes.support_ironing_flow: How much plastic ironing on the support interface lays down, in percent of a normal line. Too much leaves ridges; too little does not flatten the surface.
notes.support_ironing_pattern: The path the nozzle follows when ironing the support interface.
notes.support_ironing_spacing: The gap between ironing passes on the support interface, in mm. Smaller is smoother and slower.
notes.tree_support_brim_width: Width of the brim under each tree support trunk, in mm. A wider brim keeps tall, thin trees from tipping over.
notes.bottom_solid_infill_flow_ratio: Scales the plastic on bottom solid layers, on top of the filament's flow ratio. Tune it only after the main flow ratio is calibrated.
notes.extrusion_rate_smoothing_external_perime: Applies extrusion rate smoothing only to outer walls and overhangs, where speed changes show, and leaves the rest of the print at full speed.
notes.first_layer_flow_ratio: Scales the plastic on the first layer, except brims and skirts. Raise it slightly if the first layer has gaps; lower it if it ridges up.
notes.gap_fill_flow_ratio: Scales the plastic used to fill thin gaps between walls, on top of the filament's flow ratio.
notes.inner_wall_flow_ratio: Scales the plastic on inner walls, on top of the filament's flow ratio.
notes.interlocking_beam: Where two filaments meet inside a part, weaves them together with small beams so the materials grip each other. Helps materials that don't bond, such as PLA and TPU.
notes.interlocking_beam_layer_count: How many layers tall each interlocking beam is. Taller beams interlock more coarsely.
notes.interlocking_beam_width: Width of each interlocking beam, in mm. Wider beams are stronger and coarser.
notes.interlocking_boundary_avoidance: Keeps interlocking beams this many beam widths away from the outside of the part, so the weave stays hidden.
notes.interlocking_depth: How far the interlocking weave reaches into each material, counted in beams.
notes.interlocking_orientation: The angle the interlocking beams run at, in degrees, in the XY plane.
notes.internal_solid_infill_flow_ratio: Scales the plastic on solid infill inside the part, on top of the filament's flow ratio.
notes.max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope: Limits how fast the flow may change, in mm3/s per second, so sudden speed changes leave no bulges or gaps. 0 turns it off; slow printers without pressure advance start around 10 to 15.
notes.max_volumetric_extrusion_rate_slope_segm: Length of the steps a smoothed line is cut into, in mm. Shorter steps change the flow more smoothly but make the G-code larger; raise it if the printer stutters.
notes.mmu_segmented_region_interlocking_depth: On every other layer, painted colors reach this much deeper, in mm, so the two filaments interlock. 0 turns it off.
notes.mmu_segmented_region_max_width: How far painted colors reach in from the outside of the part, in mm; the inside prints in the part's own filament, which saves filament. 0 fills the whole painted region.
notes.outer_wall_flow_ratio: Scales the plastic on the outer wall, on top of the filament's flow ratio. Lower it a little for a crisper surface if walls bulge.
notes.overhang_flow_ratio: Scales the plastic on overhangs and bridges, on top of the filament's flow ratio. Slightly lower can reduce sagging.
notes.print_flow_ratio: Scales every extrusion in this process by the same amount. Keep it between 0.95 and 1.05 and calibrate the filament flow first.
notes.scarf_joint_flow_ratio: Scales the plastic on the ramped part of a scarf seam. Lower it if the seam bulges.
notes.set_other_flow_ratios: Shows separate flow ratios for each kind of line (walls, infill, support and so on). Leave it off unless one kind of line needs its own tuning.
notes.small_area_infill_flow_compensation: Lowers the flow of short solid infill lines, which tend to over-extrude in small areas. The small area flow model sets how much.
notes.small_area_infill_flow_compensation_mode: Pairs of line length in mm and flow factor, one pair per line, shortest first. A line takes the factor for its length, blended between points, and full flow past the last length.
notes.sparse_infill_flow_ratio: Scales the plastic on sparse infill, on top of the filament's flow ratio.
notes.support_flow_ratio: Scales the plastic on support and raft, on top of the filament's flow ratio. Lower makes support easier to break away.
notes.support_interface_flow_ratio: Scales the plastic on the support interface, the dense layers touching the part.
notes.top_solid_infill_flow_ratio: Scales the plastic on top surfaces, on top of the filament's flow ratio. Lowering it a few percent can give a smoother top.
notes.exclude_object: Writes object labels the firmware understands (EXCLUDE_OBJECT), so you can cancel one failed part and let the rest finish. Needs Klipper or another firmware that supports it.
notes.filename_format: The name of the exported G-code file. Placeholders in braces fill in when slicing ends, such as {input_filename_base}, {plate_name} and {print_time}.
notes.gcode_add_line_number: Puts N1, N2 and so on in front of every G-code command, for printers and hosts that check line numbers. Most printers don't need it.
notes.gcode_comments: Adds a comment to G-code lines saying what each one does. Useful for reading the file; it makes the file larger, which can slow printing from an SD card.
notes.gcode_label_objects: Marks which object each move belongs to, so a print host such as OctoPrint can cancel a single object.
notes.notes: Your own notes about this process profile. They are written as comments at the top of the G-code.
notes.post_process: Scripts run on the G-code after slicing, one absolute path per line. Each gets the file path as its first argument.
notes.process_change_extrusion_role_gcode: G-code written each time the print moves to another feature, such as outer wall or sparse infill, after the printer's and the filament's own.
notes.accel_to_decel_enable: On Klipper, sets max_accel_to_decel with each acceleration change, so short moves don't reach the full acceleration. Smoother and slightly slower.
notes.accel_to_decel_factor: On Klipper, the deceleration limit as a percent of the acceleration. Lower is gentler on short zigzag moves.
notes.bridge_acceleration: Acceleration on bridges, in mm/s2 or as a percent of the outer wall acceleration. Lower keeps bridge strands from being yanked loose.
notes.default_acceleration: Acceleration for printing moves that have no setting of their own, in mm/s2. Higher saves time and adds ringing; lower is quieter and cleaner.
notes.default_jerk: Jerk for moves that have no setting of their own, in mm/s: the speed change allowed instantly at a corner. 0 leaves the firmware's value.
notes.default_junction_deviation: Marlin's junction deviation, which replaces jerk on newer Marlin. Larger values take corners faster with more ringing; 0 leaves the firmware's value.
notes.infill_jerk: Jerk for infill, in mm/s. Higher is faster at corners and shakes the printer more.
notes.initial_layer_acceleration: Acceleration on the first layer, in mm/s2. Lower helps lines stick to the bed.
notes.initial_layer_jerk: Jerk on the first layer, in mm/s. Lower is gentler and helps adhesion.
notes.initial_layer_travel_acceleration: Acceleration of travel moves on the first layer, in mm/s2 or as a percent of travel acceleration. Lower keeps freshly laid lines from being knocked loose.
notes.initial_layer_travel_jerk: Jerk of travel moves on the first layer, in mm/s or as a percent of travel jerk.
notes.inner_wall_acceleration: Acceleration on inner walls, in mm/s2. Inner walls don't show, so this can be higher than the outer wall's.
notes.inner_wall_jerk: Jerk on inner walls, in mm/s.
notes.internal_solid_infill_acceleration: Acceleration on solid infill inside the part, in mm/s2 or as a percent of the default acceleration.
notes.outer_wall_acceleration: Acceleration on the outer wall, in mm/s2. Lower gives cleaner corners with less ringing; higher saves time.
notes.outer_wall_jerk: Jerk on the outer wall, in mm/s. Lower softens corners and reduces ringing.
notes.sparse_infill_acceleration: Acceleration on sparse infill, in mm/s2 or as a percent of the default acceleration. Infill doesn't show, so this can be high.
notes.top_surface_acceleration: Acceleration on top surfaces, in mm/s2. Lower can make top skins smoother.
notes.top_surface_jerk: Jerk on top surfaces, in mm/s.
notes.travel_acceleration: Acceleration of moves that don't print, in mm/s2. Higher saves time and gives less time to ooze; too high can shake the part or skip steps.
notes.travel_jerk: Jerk of moves that don't print, in mm/s.
notes.bottom_surface_filament_id: Which filament prints the bottom surface. Default uses the part's own filament.
notes.enable_prime_tower: Builds a tower beside the parts where the nozzle purges the old color after each filament change, so the parts stay clean. Needed for most multi-color prints; it costs filament and time.
notes.enable_tower_interface_cooldown_during_t: When the interface temperature boost is on, drops the nozzle back to print temperature at the start of the prime tower. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.enable_tower_interface_features: Turns on special prime tower handling where two different materials meet. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.flush_into_infill: Purges some of the old color into the parts' infill after a filament change, which saves filament and time. SlicerX does this by default when the profile doesn't say; turn it off if a clear outer wall would show mixed infill.
notes.flush_into_objects: Purges into this whole object after a filament change, so it comes out in mixed colors. Use it for a throwaway part that only exists to take the purge.
notes.flush_into_support: Purges some of the old color into support after a filament change, which saves filament and time. On by default.
notes.inner_wall_filament_id: Which filament prints the inner walls. Default uses the part's own filament.
notes.internal_solid_filament_id: Which filament prints solid infill inside the part. Default uses the part's own filament.
notes.ooze_prevention: Lowers the temperature of extruders that aren't printing, so they don't drip on the part. For multi-extruder printers.
notes.outer_wall_filament_id: Which filament prints the outer wall. Default uses the part's own filament.
notes.prime_tower_brim_width: Width of the brim around the prime tower, in mm. A negative value sizes it from the tower's height; a brim keeps tall towers from tipping.
notes.prime_tower_enable_framework: Adds internal ribs to steady the prime tower. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.prime_tower_flat_ironing: Irons the top of the prime tower flat. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.prime_tower_infill_gap: Spacing of the prime tower's sparse infill, in percent of a line width. Larger saves filament and makes a weaker tower.
notes.prime_tower_skip_points: Lets the nozzle skip the tower's travel points when it has nothing to purge. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.prime_tower_width: Width of the prime tower, in mm. A wider tower is steadier and takes more bed space.
notes.prime_tower_auto_position: atlas puts the prime tower on a free spot next to the parts, clear of the printer's no-go areas, and widens it when nothing else fits. Turn it off to keep the tower where you put it.
notes.single_extruder_multi_material_priming: Primes every filament in a line along the front of the bed at the start. For single-nozzle multi-material printers.
notes.sparse_infill_filament_id: Which filament prints sparse infill. Default uses the part's own filament; a cheaper filament here can save money.
notes.standby_temperature_delta: How much an idle extruder cools while another prints, in degrees C. Negative values cool it; ignored when the filament sets its own idle temperature.
notes.support_filament: Which filament prints the support and raft. Default uses the part's filament; a soluble or breakaway filament makes support easier to remove.
notes.support_interface_filament: Which filament prints the support interface, the layers that touch the part. A separate interface filament gives a clean underside with little waste.
notes.toolchange_cyclic_first_layer: Applies the cyclic tool change order on the first layer too. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.toolchange_cyclic_order: The order tools cycle through with cyclic tool changes. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.toolchange_ordering: How the order of tool changes on each layer is picked. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.top_surface_filament_id: Which filament prints the top surface. Default uses the part's own filament.
notes.wipe_tower_bridging: The longest unsupported span in the prime tower's sparse layers, in mm.
notes.wipe_tower_cone_angle: Widens the prime tower's base into a cone for stability; larger angles make a wider base. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.wipe_tower_extra_flow: Extra flow on the purge lines in the prime tower, in percent. Thicker lines purge faster and make a sturdier tower.
notes.wipe_tower_extra_rib_length: Lengthens the prime tower's ribs past its corners, in mm. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.wipe_tower_extra_spacing: Spacing of the purge lines in the prime tower, in percent of normal. Wider spacing uses less filament per layer.
notes.wipe_tower_filament: Which filament prints the outline of the prime tower. 0 picks one that is available, preferring a non-soluble one.
notes.wipe_tower_fillet_wall: Rounds the corners of the prime tower walls. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.wipe_tower_max_purge_speed: The fastest the prime tower prints while purging, in mm/s. The filament's flow limit may hold it lower.
notes.wipe_tower_no_sparse_layers: Skips prime tower layers that have no tool change, which saves filament. The nozzle then drops down to the tower, so make sure nothing on the plate is in the way.
notes.wipe_tower_rib_width: Width of the ribs that brace the prime tower, in mm. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.wipe_tower_rotation_angle: Turns the prime tower on the bed, in degrees from the X axis. Useful when a long tower fits the free space better at an angle.
notes.wipe_tower_sparse_layers_combination: Combines several sparse prime tower layers into one taller layer. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.wipe_tower_wall_type: The outer wall shape of the prime tower: a plain rectangle, a cone that widens at the base, or ribs that brace the sides. Cones and ribs keep tall, narrow towers standing.
notes.bridge_angle: Forces the direction bridge lines run, in degrees; 0 picks the best direction for each bridge. SlicerX always picks the direction itself and keeps this value only for profile exchange.
notes.bridge_density: How closely bridge lines sit, in percent. Above 100 the lines overlap for a smoother underside; below 100 they get room to cool, which can help on long spans.
notes.bridge_flow: Scales the plastic in bridge lines. Lower gives thinner lines that sag less; higher makes stronger lines that touch each other better.
notes.bridge_line_width: Line width on bridges, in mm or as a percent of the nozzle diameter, at most the nozzle size. Narrower lines cool faster and sag less.
notes.bridge_no_support: Leaves bridges without support underneath, since short bridges print fine in mid-air. Saves support material; long bridges may sag.
notes.bridge_speed: Print speed for bridges you can see from outside, in mm/s. Slower lets each strand cool and hold its shape; 20 to 50 mm/s is typical.
notes.counterbore_hole_bridging: Bridges the step of a counterbore hole so it prints without support. Partially bridge covers only part of the opening; sacrificial layer prints a full layer you drill out after printing.
notes.detect_overhang_wall: Measures how far each wall hangs out past the layer below and slows down to match, reaching bridge speed for a wall with nothing under it.
notes.enable_overhang_speed: Slows walls down in steps as they hang further out, using the four overhang speeds. Turn it off to print overhangs at full wall speed.
notes.extra_perimeters_on_overhangs: Adds wall loops over steep overhangs and around bridges that have nothing to anchor to. Helps them print cleanly at the cost of some time.
notes.make_overhang_printable: Changes the model so steep overhangs become printable without support, by filling under them with cones of material. The part's shape changes.
notes.make_overhang_printable_angle: The steepest overhang left after the model is reshaped, in degrees from vertical. 90 leaves the model alone; lower fills more material in under overhangs.
notes.make_overhang_printable_hole_size: Holes in the bottom of the model smaller than this area, in mm2, are filled with cones when overhangs are made printable. 0 fills every hole.
notes.overhang_1_4_speed: Speed for walls that hang out up to a quarter of a line width, in mm/s or as a percent of wall speed. 0 keeps the normal wall speed.
notes.overhang_2_4_speed: Speed for walls that hang out a quarter to half a line width, in mm/s or as a percent of wall speed. 0 keeps the normal wall speed.
notes.overhang_3_4_speed: Speed for walls that hang out half to three quarters of a line width, in mm/s or as a percent of wall speed. 0 keeps the normal wall speed.
notes.overhang_4_4_speed: Speed for walls that hang out three quarters of a line width or more, in mm/s or as a percent of wall speed. 0 keeps the normal wall speed.
notes.overhang_reverse: On every other layer, prints walls over an overhang in the opposite direction. This can greatly improve steep overhangs and reduces warping.
notes.overhang_reverse_internal_only: Reverses only the inner walls on alternate layers, which spreads stress to reduce warping and keeps the outer wall's finish. Good for ABS, ASA and flexible filaments.
notes.overhang_reverse_threshold: How far a wall must hang out before it is reversed, in mm or as a percent of the line width. 0 reverses on every other layer regardless.
notes.thick_bridges: Prints bridges as round strands as thick as the nozzle, which are stronger and span further. They look rougher than thin bridges.
notes.detect_thin_wall: Prints walls too thin for two lines as a single line. SlicerX ignores it: aegis and Arachne already print thin features with variable-width walls.
notes.dont_filter_internal_bridges: Which small internal bridges are dropped so solid infill prints straight over the sparse infill. Filter suits most parts; limited and no filtering add bridges under slanted tops, reducing pillowing.
notes.elefant_foot_compensation: Shrinks the first layer inward by this much, in mm, to undo the bulge that forms where the part is pressed onto the bed. 0.1 to 0.2 mm is typical.
notes.elefant_foot_compensation_layers: How many bottom layers get elephant foot compensation, tapering off upward.
notes.elefant_foot_layers_density: Infill density of the layers that get elephant foot compensation, in percent. Lower leaves the squished layers room to spread.
notes.enable_arc_fitting: Writes curves as G2 and G3 arc moves instead of many short lines, making smaller files that some printers run more smoothly. Leave it off on Klipper, which splits arcs back into lines.
notes.enable_extra_bridge_layer: Prints a second bridge layer over bridges, so the solid layers above sag less and the top shows less pillowing. Costs a little time per bridge.
notes.enable_mixed_color_sublayer: Prints mixed colors in thinner sublayers. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filter_out_gap_fill: Skips gap fill lines shorter than this, in mm. Raising it saves time on many tiny moves and can leave small gaps.
notes.hole_to_polyhole: Prints round vertical holes as polygons with fewer, flat sides sized to the nozzle. Holes come out closer to their true size, which helps with pins and screws.
notes.hole_to_polyhole_max_edges: The most sides a polyhole may have. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.hole_to_polyhole_threshold: How far a hole's points may stray from a true circle and still count as round, in mm or as a percent of the radius.
notes.hole_to_polyhole_twisted: Turns each polyhole a little every layer, so the flat sides don't line up and the hole stays round on average.
notes.initial_layer_line_width: Line width on the first layer, in mm or as a percent of the nozzle diameter. Wider first lines grip the bed better; 0 uses the default line width.
notes.initial_layer_min_bead_width: The narrowest wall line allowed on the first layer, as a percent of the nozzle diameter. Close to 100 helps thin features stick.
notes.initial_layer_print_height: Height of the first layer, in mm. A thicker first layer is more forgiving of a bed that isn't perfectly level; 0.2 mm suits a 0.4 mm nozzle.
notes.inner_wall_line_width: Line width of inner walls, in mm or as a percent of the nozzle diameter. 0 uses the default line width.
notes.internal_bridge_flow: Scales the plastic in internal bridges, the first solid layer over sparse infill. Raising it can strengthen the layers above and improve the top surface.
notes.internal_solid_infill_line_width: Line width of solid infill inside the part, in mm or as a percent of the nozzle diameter. 0 uses the default line width.
notes.ironing_angle: The direction ironing lines run, in degrees. Used when the ironing angle is fixed.
notes.ironing_angle_fixed: Irons at the fixed ironing angle instead of following the top surface's lines.
notes.ironing_expansion: Grows or shrinks the ironed area, in mm. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.ironing_flow: How much plastic ironing lays down, in percent of a normal layer. Around 10 to 15 percent fills small gaps; too much leaves a rough, ridged top.
notes.ironing_inset: Keeps ironing this far inside the edge of the top surface, in mm, so the edges don't get a raised lip.
notes.ironing_pattern: The path the nozzle follows when ironing.
notes.ironing_spacing: The gap between ironing passes, in mm. Smaller is smoother and takes longer.
notes.ironing_speed: Speed of the ironing passes, in mm/s. Slower gives a smoother top.
notes.ironing_type: After a top surface prints, runs the hot nozzle over it again with a little plastic to smooth it. Topmost irons only the very top; it adds noticeable time.
notes.is_infill_first: Prints infill before the walls on each layer. This can help steep overhangs, but the infill may push the walls out and show through the surface.
notes.layer_height: The height of each layer, in mm. Thinner layers give smoother curves and slopes but take longer; keep it within 25 to 75 percent of the nozzle diameter.
notes.line_width: The width of every line that has no width of its own, in mm or as a percent of the nozzle diameter. 0 uses the nozzle diameter.
notes.max_travel_detour_distance: When avoiding walls, the longest detour allowed, in mm or as a percent of the direct path. Longer detours are skipped; 0 sets no limit.
notes.min_bead_width: The narrowest wall line aegis or Arachne may print, as a percent of the nozzle diameter. Thin features are widened to at least this.
notes.min_feature_size: Features thinner than this are dropped, as a percent of the nozzle diameter; anything thicker is printed at least the min bead width.
notes.min_length_factor: Drops short, unclosed walls that cost time and add little, in mm. Higher removes more and longer ones; top and bottom surfaces are not affected.
notes.min_width_top_surface: A top area narrower than this doesn't count as a top surface, in mm or as a percent of the line width, so the single top wall doesn't kick in on small ledges.
notes.only_one_wall_first_layer: Prints just one wall on the first layer, leaving more room for the bottom pattern.
notes.only_one_wall_top: Prints just one wall on flat top surfaces, leaving more room for the top pattern, which can look cleaner.
notes.outer_wall_line_width: Line width of the outer wall, in mm or as a percent of the nozzle diameter. Slightly narrower can give finer detail; 0 uses the default line width.
notes.precise_outer_wall: Adjusts the spacing between the outer wall and the next one so the outside dimensions come out more accurately. Ignored when the outer wall prints first.
notes.precise_z_height: Adjusts the last few layer heights so the top of the part lands exactly at the model's height.
notes.scarf_angle_threshold: With conditional scarf seams, a loop with no corner sharper than this angle gets a scarf seam, in degrees. Loops with a sharp corner hide the seam there instead.
notes.scarf_joint_speed: Speed of the ramped part of a scarf seam, in mm/s or as a percent of the wall speed. Slower, under 100 mm/s, gives a cleaner seam.
notes.scarf_overhang_threshold: A scarf seam is used only where less than this much of the wall hangs out, as a percent of the line width.
notes.seam_gap: Stops each loop this far short of where it started, in mm or as a percent of the nozzle diameter, which hides the blob where the ends meet.
notes.seam_position: Where each wall loop starts and ends, which leaves a small mark. Aligned lines the marks up in one seam, back puts it at the rear, random scatters it; nearest saves travel.
notes.seam_slope_conditional: Uses a scarf seam only on smooth loops where a normal seam has no corner to hide in.
notes.seam_slope_entire_loop: Ramps the scarf seam along the whole loop instead of a short stretch.
notes.seam_slope_inner_walls: Uses a scarf seam on inner walls too.
notes.seam_slope_min_length: Length of the scarf seam's ramp, in mm. Longer hides the seam better; 0 turns the scarf off.
notes.seam_slope_start_height: Height where the scarf ramp starts, in mm or as a percent of the layer height. 0 starts at the bottom of the layer.
notes.seam_slope_steps: How many steps the scarf ramp is split into. More steps make a smoother ramp.
notes.seam_slope_type: Ramps the start and end of each wall loop up and over each other, so the seam blends in and holds better. Contour applies it to outer walls, contour and hole also to holes.
notes.slicing_mode: How the model is read when it has odd geometry. Even-odd suits 3DLabPrint airplane models; close holes fills every hole in the model.
notes.smart_layer: sleipnir varies the layer height up the part. Quality uses thin layers where curves and detail need them; strength thins them where the part carries load.
notes.smart_layer_max_height: The thickest layer sleipnir may use, in mm. Keep it at most three quarters of the nozzle diameter.
notes.smart_layer_max_step_ratio: The biggest change in layer height from one layer to the next, as a fraction of the previous layer. Smaller steps look smoother.
notes.smart_layer_min_height: The thinnest layer sleipnir may use, in mm. Keep it at least a quarter of the nozzle diameter.
notes.smart_layer_smoothing: How strongly sleipnir blends neighboring layer heights, in percent. 0 follows the surface exactly; 100 gives the gentlest change.
notes.smart_layer_smoothing_radius: How far up and down the part sleipnir blends layer heights, in mm. 0 picks eight times the thickest layer.
notes.sparse_infill_line_width: Line width of sparse infill, in mm or as a percent of the nozzle diameter. Wider lines fill faster and make stronger infill.
notes.staggered_inner_seams: Shifts the seams of inner walls back a little more for each wall, in a zigzag, so they don't stack into one weak line.
notes.support_line_width: Line width of support, in mm or as a percent of the nozzle diameter. 0 uses the default line width.
notes.thick_internal_bridges: Prints the first solid layer over sparse infill as thick strands as tall as the nozzle, which bridge the infill gaps more reliably.
notes.top_surface_line_width: Line width of top surfaces, in mm or as a percent of the nozzle diameter. Narrower lines give a finer top finish.
notes.top_surface_pattern: The line pattern on top surfaces. Monotonic lays every line in the same order for an even sheen; concentric and the curve patterns are decorative.
notes.tree_support_auto_brim: Sizes the brim under tree supports automatically, from how tall the branches are.
notes.unsupported_wall_last: Prints walls that rest on nothing after the walls beside them. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.wall_direction: The direction outer wall loops print in, seen from above. Holes print the other way; switching it can move where small blobs show up.
notes.wall_distribution_count: How many walls, counted from the center, share the width changes aegis or Arachne make. Lower keeps the outer walls an even width.
notes.wall_generator: How walls are laid out. aegis (the default) varies wall width to fit the part, so thin features print solid and walls stay even; Arachne does the same with more width changes, and classic keeps one width.
notes.wall_maximum_deviation: How far simplified walls may stray from the model, in mm. Larger makes smaller G-code and slightly less accurate walls.
notes.wall_maximum_resolution: The shortest wall segment kept, in mm. Smaller keeps finer detail and makes larger G-code.
notes.wall_sequence: Which walls print first on each layer. Inner then outer gives the best outer surface; outer first is more accurate; inner, outer, inner is a middle ground.
notes.wall_transition_angle: Where a wedge gets thin, how sharp it must be before the number of walls changes, in degrees. Lower leaves fewer extra center walls but may leave gaps.
notes.wall_transition_filter_deviation: A margin that stops walls switching back and forth between one more and one fewer line. Larger means fewer switches, fewer starts and stops.
notes.wall_transition_length: How much room a change in the number of walls is given, as a percent of the nozzle diameter.
notes.wipe_before_external_loop: Starts the outer wall a little inside its start point, so any extra plastic from restarting stays hidden. Helps when the outer wall prints after an inner one.
notes.wipe_inward: Wipes the nozzle inward at the end of a loop. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.wipe_inward_distance: How far the inward wipe goes. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.wipe_on_loops: Moves the nozzle a little inward before it leaves a closed loop, which makes the seam less visible.
notes.xy_contour_compensation: Grows or shrinks the outside of the part in X and Y, in mm. Use small values, such as -0.05, when printed parts come out too large to fit.
notes.xy_hole_compensation: Grows or shrinks holes in X and Y, in mm. Positive values make holes bigger; use it when pins and screws don't fit.
notes.zaa_dont_alternate_fill_direction: Keeps the fill direction the same on every layer when Z contouring. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.zaa_enabled: Z contouring prints the top of curved surfaces with tilted paths to smooth out stair steps. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.zaa_min_z: The thinnest layer for Z contouring, in mm. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.zaa_minimize_perimeter_height: Lowers top walls to match the model edge where the slope is gentler than this angle. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.reduce_crossing_wall: Routes travel moves around walls instead of across them, so oozing leaves fewer marks on the surface. Travel takes a little longer.
notes.reduce_infill_retraction: Skips retraction when a travel stays inside infill, where oozing can't be seen. Saves time on busy parts.
notes.enable_wrapping_detection: Runs the wrapping detection G-code on every layer, on printers that can detect filament wrapping around the nozzle.
notes.fuzzy_skin: Jitters the nozzle while printing walls, which gives the part a rough, textured surface that hides layer lines. Choose which walls get the texture.
notes.fuzzy_skin_first_layer: Applies fuzzy skin on the first layer too. Usually left off so the base stays flat against the bed.
notes.fuzzy_skin_layers_between_ripple_offset: How many layers share the same ripple position before it shifts.
notes.fuzzy_skin_mode: How the texture is made: displacement moves the nozzle sideways, extrusion varies the amount of plastic, combined does both.
notes.fuzzy_skin_noise_type: The shape of the texture. Classic is random; Perlin and billow are smoother and more even; ridged, Voronoi and ripple make marble, cell and wave looks.
notes.fuzzy_skin_octaves: How many layers of detail the noise has. More gives finer texture.
notes.fuzzy_skin_persistence: How much the finer layers of noise count. Lower gives a smoother texture.
notes.fuzzy_skin_point_distance: Average distance between the jitter points along the wall, in mm. Smaller gives a finer texture and larger G-code.
notes.fuzzy_skin_ripple_offset: How far the ripples shift along the wall each layer group, in percent of a wave. 50 alternates them; 0 stacks them in straight lines.
notes.fuzzy_skin_ripples_per_layer: How many full ripples wrap around each layer.
notes.fuzzy_skin_scale: The size of the texture's features, in mm. Larger values make bigger bumps.
notes.fuzzy_skin_thickness: How far the nozzle wanders in and out, in mm. Keep it below the outer wall line width; 0.2 to 0.4 mm is typical.
notes.preheat_time: Starts heating the next tool this many seconds before it's needed, so a tool change doesn't wait. For printers with several heated tools.
notes.print_order: The order objects print in within each layer. Default lets the slicer choose; as object list follows the order in the object list.
notes.print_sequence: By layer prints all parts together, one layer at a time. By object finishes each part before starting the next, which limits stringing between parts but needs room around the toolhead.
notes.spiral_finishing_flow_ratio: Flow at the very end of a vase print, where it normally tapers to zero. Raise it if the top edge comes out thin.
notes.spiral_mode: Prints the part as one continuous spiral with a single wall and a solid bottom, rising steadily so there is no seam. For vases and lamp shades; the part comes out hollow with no top.
notes.spiral_mode_max_xy_smoothing: How far smooth spiral may move points sideways to even out the spiral, in mm or as a percent of the nozzle diameter.
notes.spiral_mode_smooth: Also smooths sideways moves in spiral vase mode, so no seam shows even on slanted walls.
notes.spiral_starting_flow_ratio: Flow at the very start of the spiral, where it normally ramps up from zero over the first loop. Raise it if the first loop is thin.
notes.timelapse_type: How the timelapse camera takes its shots. Traditional snaps where the toolhead is; smooth parks the toolhead out of view for each shot, which takes longer and may need a prime tower.
notes.gap_infill_speed: Speed for filling thin gaps, in mm/s. Gaps vary in width, so slower than normal infill prints them more evenly.
notes.initial_layer_infill_speed: Speed of solid infill on the first layer, in mm/s. Slower helps it stick to the bed.
notes.initial_layer_speed: Speed of walls and everything except solid infill on the first layer, in mm/s. Slower gives the first layer time to stick.
notes.initial_layer_travel_speed: Speed of travel moves on the first layer, in mm/s or as a percent of travel speed.
notes.inner_wall_speed: Speed of inner walls, in mm/s. They don't show, so they can print faster than the outer wall.
notes.internal_bridge_speed: Speed of internal bridges over sparse infill, in mm/s or as a percent of bridge speed.
notes.internal_solid_infill_speed: Speed of solid infill inside the part, not the top or bottom surface, in mm/s.
notes.outer_wall_speed: Speed of the outer wall, the surface you see, in mm/s. Slower gives a cleaner surface; this has the largest effect on looks of any speed.
notes.role_based_wipe_speed: Wipes at the speed of the line just printed instead of the fixed wipe speed.
notes.slow_down_layers: Ramps the speed up gradually over this many layers after the first one, which helps tall, narrow parts stay stuck to the bed.
notes.slowdown_for_curled_perimeters: Slows walls down where the layer below may have curled up, such as sharp overhanging corners, so the nozzle doesn't catch them.
notes.small_perimeter_speed: Speed for small loops such as small holes, in mm/s or as a percent of outer wall speed. Slower gives rounder small features.
notes.small_perimeter_threshold: Loops shorter than this, in mm, count as small and use the small perimeter speed.
notes.small_support_perimeter_speed: Speed for small support loops, in mm/s or as a percent of the support speed. 0 uses half speed.
notes.small_support_perimeter_threshold: Support loops shorter than this, in mm, use the small support perimeter speed.
notes.sparse_infill_speed: Speed of sparse infill, in mm/s. Usually high, since infill doesn't show; the filament's flow limit may hold it lower.
notes.support_interface_speed: Speed of the support interface, the dense layers touching the part, in mm/s. Slower gives a cleaner underside.
notes.top_surface_speed: Speed of the top surface, in mm/s. Slower gives a smoother, more even top.
notes.travel_speed: Speed of moves that don't print, in mm/s. Faster saves time and gives plastic less time to ooze.
notes.wipe_speed: Speed of the wipe move, in mm/s or as a percent of travel speed.
notes.align_infill_direction_to_model: Turns the infill and the fixed bridge angles with the model when you rotate it on the plate, so the lines keep the same direction on the part.
notes.alternate_extra_wall: Adds an extra wall on every other layer, so the infill locks between the walls for a stronger part. Turn off keep shells thick on steep sides when using it.
notes.bottom_layer_direction: Fixes the direction of the bottom layer's lines, in degrees; -1 uses the solid infill direction. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.bottom_shell_layers: Number of solid layers on the bottom of the part. More gives a stronger, more watertight bottom and uses more filament.
notes.bottom_shell_thickness: The least thickness of the solid bottom, in mm. Layers are added when the bottom shell layers come out thinner than this, such as with thin layers; 0 turns it off.
notes.bottom_surface_density: How densely the bottom surface is filled, in percent. 100 gives a solid bottom; lower values space the lines out and save filament.
notes.bottom_surface_fill_order: Whether the bottom surface fills from the center out or from the edge in. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.bottom_surface_pattern: The line pattern on the bottom surface, the side that sits on the bed.
notes.center_of_surface_pattern: Where centered patterns such as concentric and spirals are centered. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.detect_narrow_internal_solid_infill: Fills narrow strips of solid infill with a concentric pattern, which is faster than many short back-and-forth lines.
notes.ensure_vertical_shell_thickness: Adds solid infill near sloped surfaces so the shell is as thick on slopes as on flat tops. All is safest; critical only and none save filament but can leave thin spots.
notes.extra_solid_infills: Layers whose sparse infill prints solid, to stiffen tall parts: list layer numbers like 1,7,9, or 5 for every fifth layer. Leave empty for none.
notes.fill_multiline: Prints each infill line as several side-by-side lines. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.gap_fill_target: Which solid surfaces get gap fill, the thin lines that close slivers between wall and fill. Top and bottom closes visible pinholes; everywhere also fills inside.
notes.gyroid_optimized: Shortens the gyroid's waves along the height at low densities, below about 30 percent, so the infill resists crushing from above better for about the same filament.
notes.infill_anchor: How far an infill line continues along the wall to anchor itself, in mm or as a percent of the infill line width. Anchors make infill stronger and stick to the walls better.
notes.infill_anchor_max: The longest anchor along the wall an infill line may have, in mm or as a percent of the infill line spacing. 0 turns anchoring off.
notes.infill_combination: Prints the sparse infill once every few layers as one thicker layer, to save time. Walls still print at the normal layer height.
notes.infill_combination_max_layer_height: The tallest combined sparse infill layer, in mm or as a percent of the nozzle diameter. 100 percent lets the infill reach the nozzle diameter; about 80 is stronger.
notes.infill_direction: The angle the sparse infill lines start from, in degrees.
notes.infill_lock_depth: How deep the locked zag pattern's interlocking skin reaches, in mm.
notes.infill_overhang_angle: The overhang angle of the lateral honeycomb's sloped walls, in degrees. Steeper prints faster but needs good cooling.
notes.infill_shift_step: How far cross zag and locked zag shift their lines each layer, in mm.
notes.infill_wall_overlap: How far sparse infill reaches into the walls, in percent of the infill line width, so they bond. 10 to 15 percent bonds well without blobs.
notes.interface_shells: On parts printed in more than one filament, gives each filament region its own solid top and bottom where it meets another. Off lets the infill run across the border.
notes.internal_bridge_angle: Forces the direction internal bridge lines run, in degrees; 0 picks the best direction for each bridge.
notes.internal_bridge_density: How closely internal bridge lines sit, in percent. Above 100 they support the top layers better; below 100 they print faster with more sag.
notes.internal_solid_infill_pattern: The line pattern of solid infill inside the part.
notes.lateral_lattice_angle_1: The angle of the first set of lateral lattice bars, in degrees from vertical.
notes.lateral_lattice_angle_2: The angle of the second set of lateral lattice bars, in degrees from vertical.
notes.lightning_overhang_angle: How steep lightning infill may hang out from below, in degrees. Larger angles use less infill; too large and the top may sag.
notes.lightning_prune_angle: How far lightning infill branches are trimmed back, as an angle. Larger angles trim more and save filament.
notes.lightning_straightening_angle: How much lightning infill branches are straightened, as an angle. Larger angles give straighter, shorter branches.
notes.minimum_sparse_infill_area: Sparse infill areas smaller than this, in mm2, print solid instead. Small solid areas are stronger and avoid many tiny moves.
notes.relative_bridge_angle: Adds the bridge angle to the direction picked for each bridge instead of replacing it.
notes.separated_infills: Prints the infill of each region separately. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.skeleton_infill_density: Density of the locked zag pattern's inner skeleton, in percent.
notes.skeleton_infill_line_width: Line width of the locked zag pattern's inner skeleton, in mm or as a percent.
notes.skin_infill_density: Density of the locked zag pattern's outer skin, in percent.
notes.skin_infill_depth: How thick the locked zag pattern's outer skin is, in mm.
notes.skin_infill_line_width: Line width of the locked zag pattern's outer skin, in mm or as a percent.
notes.solid_infill_direction: The angle solid infill lines start from, in degrees.
notes.solid_infill_rotate_template: Angles for the solid infill lines, layer by layer, in degrees, such as 0,90. Leave empty to use the solid infill direction.
notes.sparse_infill_density: How much of the inside is filled, in percent. 15 to 20 suits most parts; higher is stronger and heavier, and takes longer to print.
notes.sparse_infill_pattern: The shape of the infill inside the part. Gyroid is strong in all directions; grid and rectilinear are fast; lightning uses the least plastic and only holds up the top.
notes.sparse_infill_rotate_template: Angles for the sparse infill lines, layer by layer, in degrees. 0,90 alternates two directions, and +5 turns the lines 5 degrees more every layer.
notes.sparse_infill_smooth_factor: Rounds the corners of sparse infill paths. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.symmetric_infill_y_axis: Mirrors the infill across the Y axis. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.top_bottom_infill_wall_overlap: How far the first and topmost solid layers reach into the walls, in percent. More overlap closes pinholes along the wall; too much makes the edge bulge.
notes.top_layer_direction: Fixes the direction of the top layer's lines, in degrees; -1 uses the solid infill direction.
notes.top_shell_layers: Number of solid layers on top of the part. More layers close the top better over sparse infill; 4 or 5 at 0.2 mm is typical.
notes.top_shell_thickness: The least thickness of the solid top, in mm. Layers are added when the top shell layers come out thinner than this, such as with thin layers; 0 turns it off.
notes.top_surface_density: How densely the top surface is filled, in percent. 100 gives a solid, smooth top; lower values space the lines out, and 0 leaves the top open.
notes.top_surface_expansion: Grows the top surface past its outline, in mm. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.top_surface_expansion_direction: Which way the top surface grows. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.top_surface_expansion_margin: A margin for top surface growth, in mm. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.top_surface_fill_order: Whether the top surface fills from the center out or from the edge in. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.wall_loops: How many outlines each layer gets around the outside and around holes. More loops make stronger, heavier parts and take longer; 2 to 3 suits most prints.
notes.combine_brims: Merges brims that sit close together into one, so neighboring parts hold each other down.
notes.enable_support: Builds removable support under overhangs that would otherwise print in mid-air. Supports cost filament and time and leave marks where they touch the part.
notes.independent_support_layer_height: Lets support use its own layer height, which saves time and allows a finer gap under the part. Not used when the prime tower is on.
notes.max_bridge_length: Bridges up to this long, in mm, print without support. 0 supports every bridge.
notes.support_angle: Turns the support pattern on the bed, in degrees.
notes.support_base_pattern: The pattern inside the support. Lightning grows thin branches that hold up only what needs it; hollow prints tree branches with walls only.
notes.support_base_pattern_spacing: The gap between support lines, in mm. Wider spacing uses less filament and is easier to remove but holds the part less firmly.
notes.support_bottom_interface_spacing: The gap between bottom interface lines, where support rests on the part, in mm. 0 makes a solid interface.
notes.support_bottom_z_distance: The vertical gap where support rests on top of the part, in mm. A gap keeps the support from fusing to the part.
notes.support_critical_regions_only: Supports only sharp tails, cantilevers and other areas that would fail outright, not every overhang.
notes.support_expansion: Grows (positive) or shrinks (negative) support sideways, in mm.
notes.support_interface_bottom_layers: Dense layers where support rests on the part, so it leaves a cleaner mark. -1 uses the same count as the top interface.
notes.support_interface_loop_pattern: Covers the top contact layer of the support with loops instead of lines.
notes.support_interface_not_for_body: Keeps the support interface filament out of the support body when it can. Saves an expensive or soluble filament.
notes.support_interface_pattern: The line pattern of the support interface. Default picks rectilinear, or concentric for soluble interfaces.
notes.support_interface_spacing: The gap between support interface lines, in mm. Smaller gives a smoother underside and is harder to remove; 0 makes it solid.
notes.support_interface_top_layers: Dense layers at the top of the support, right under the part, so the underside comes out smooth. 2 to 3 is typical.
notes.support_object_first_layer_gap: The sideways gap between support and the part on the first layer, in mm.
notes.support_object_xy_distance: The sideways gap between support and the part, in mm. Larger keeps support off vertical walls and is easier to remove.
notes.support_on_build_plate_only: Builds support only where it can stand on the bed, never on top of the part. Avoids support marks on the part but can leave some overhangs unsupported.
notes.support_remove_small_overhang: Skips support for small overhangs that print fine without it.
notes.support_style: The shape of the support. Grid is the stable default for normal support and snug hugs the part; organic and the tree styles merge branches to save filament.
notes.support_threshold_angle: Overhangs flatter than this angle get support, in degrees from horizontal. Lower supports fewer overhangs; 30 to 45 suits most printers.
notes.support_threshold_overlap: With a 0 threshold angle, overhangs resting on less than this much of the layer below get support, in mm or as a percent of the line width.
notes.support_top_z_distance: The vertical gap between the top of the support and the part, in mm. A larger gap breaks away more easily; a smaller one gives a cleaner underside.
notes.support_type: Normal builds straight columns under overhangs; tree grows branches that touch only where needed and use less filament. Manual builds support only where you paint it.
notes.tree_support_angle_slow: The angle branches prefer when nothing is in their way, in degrees. Lower is more upright and stable; higher merges branches sooner.
notes.tree_support_branch_angle: How far tree branches may lean, in degrees. Larger angles reach further but are less stable.
notes.tree_support_branch_angle_organic: How far organic branches may lean, in degrees. Larger angles reach further but are less stable.
notes.tree_support_branch_diameter: Thickness of tree support branches, in mm. Thicker branches are steadier and use more filament.
notes.tree_support_branch_diameter_angle: How quickly organic branches thicken toward the bottom, in degrees. A small angle makes them steadier; 0 keeps them one thickness.
notes.tree_support_branch_diameter_organic: Thickness of organic support branches, in mm.
notes.tree_support_branch_distance: How far apart tree branch tips sit, in mm. Closer tips hold the part better and are harder to remove.
notes.tree_support_branch_distance_organic: How far apart organic branch tips sit, in multiples of the tip diameter.
notes.tree_support_tip_diameter: Diameter of the branch tips that touch the part, in mm. Smaller tips leave smaller marks.
notes.tree_support_top_rate: Density of the branch tips under the part, in percent. Higher holds overhangs better and is harder to remove; interface layers are usually the better choice.
notes.tree_support_wall_count: Number of walls on tree branches, 0 to 2. 0 picks a count for you.
notes.tree_support_with_infill: Fills large hollow areas inside tree supports. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet, like Orca 2.4.2.
notes.activate_air_filtration: Runs the printer's air filtration fan, for printers that have one. Use it with materials that give off fumes, such as ABS and ASA.
notes.activate_air_filtration_during_print: Uses the exhaust fan speed set here during the print, over the speed in the filament's G-code. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.activate_air_filtration_on_completion: Uses the exhaust fan speed set here after the print, over the speed in the filament's G-code. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.additional_cooling_fan_speed: Speed of the auxiliary part cooling fan, in percent, after the first few layers. Needs the auxiliary fan turned on in the printer settings.
notes.additional_fan_full_speed_layer: The layer where the auxiliary fan reaches full speed, ramping up from the first layers. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.close_additional_fan_first_x_layers: Keeps the auxiliary fan off for this many first layers. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.close_fan_the_first_x_layers: Keeps the part cooling fan off for this many layers at the start, so the first layers stay warm and stick to the bed.
notes.complete_print_exhaust_fan_speed: Speed of the exhaust fan after the print finishes, in percent. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.dont_slow_down_outer_wall: Keeps the outer wall at full speed when a short layer is slowed to cool. Avoids changes in gloss and faint banding on the outside.
notes.during_print_exhaust_fan_speed: Speed of the exhaust fan while printing, in percent, over the speed in the filament's G-code.
notes.enable_overhang_bridge_fan: Uses a separate fan speed for overhangs and bridges, usually higher, so they set before they sag.
notes.fan_cooling_layer_time: Layers that print faster than this many seconds turn up the part cooling fan, between the minimum and maximum speed.
notes.fan_max_speed: The highest part cooling fan speed, in percent, used on the quickest layers.
notes.fan_min_speed: The lowest part cooling fan speed once the fan is on, in percent.
notes.filament_cooling_before_tower: Lowers the nozzle by this many degrees before the prime tower. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_cooling_final_speed: Final speed of the cooling moves in a single-nozzle multi-material printer, in mm/s. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_cooling_initial_speed: Starting speed of the cooling moves in a single-nozzle multi-material printer, in mm/s. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_cooling_moves: How many times the filament moves back and forth in the cooling tube before unloading. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.first_x_layer_fan_speed: Auxiliary fan speed for the first layers, in percent. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.full_fan_speed_layer: The layer where the part cooling fan reaches full speed, climbing evenly from the first layer with the fan on. 0 turns the climb off.
notes.initial_layer_fan_speed: Part cooling fan speed on the first layer, in percent; -1 follows the normal rules. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.internal_bridge_fan_speed: Part cooling fan speed on internal bridges, in percent; -1 uses the overhang fan speed. A lower speed here can reduce warping on large flat areas.
notes.ironing_fan_speed: Part cooling fan speed while ironing, in percent; -1 leaves the fan as it is. Lower can keep the nozzle from clogging at ironing's low flow.
notes.overhang_fan_speed: Part cooling fan speed on bridges and steep overhangs, in percent. More cooling sets them before they sag.
notes.overhang_fan_threshold: How much a wall must overhang before the overhang fan speed applies. Bridges always get it; at 0 percent every outer wall does.
notes.reduce_fan_stop_start_freq: Keeps the part cooling fan at least at its minimum speed instead of stopping it between layers, which spares the fan constant restarts.
notes.slow_down_for_layer_cooling: Slows printing on layers that would finish faster than the minimum layer time, so small parts and tips get time to cool. Leave it on for small details.
notes.slow_down_layer_time: Layers that would print faster than this many seconds are slowed down to give them time to cool.
notes.slow_down_min_speed: The slowest the printer goes to stretch a short layer, in mm/s. Too slow can let the nozzle ooze and blob.
notes.support_material_interface_fan_speed: Part cooling fan speed on the support interface, in percent; -1 leaves the fan as it is. Higher makes support easier to separate.
notes.filament_dev_ams_drying_ams_limitations: Limits on drying this filament in the AMS. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_dev_ams_drying_heat_distortion_: Heat distortion temperature for AMS drying, in degrees C. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_dev_ams_drying_temperature: Temperature for drying this filament in the AMS, in degrees C. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_dev_ams_drying_time: How long to dry this filament in the AMS, in hours. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_dev_chamber_drying_bed_temperat: Bed temperature for drying filament in the printer's chamber, in degrees C. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_dev_chamber_drying_time: How long to dry filament in the printer's chamber, in hours. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_dev_drying_cooling_temperature: Temperature to cool down to after drying, in degrees C. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_dev_drying_softening_temperatur: Temperature where this filament softens during drying, in degrees C. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.adaptive_pressure_advance: Changes pressure advance with speed and acceleration, using the model below, since one value rarely fits every feature. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.adaptive_pressure_advance_bridges: A separate pressure advance for bridges; 0 turns it off. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.adaptive_pressure_advance_model: Measured pressure advance values with the flow and acceleration they were measured at, one set per line. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.adaptive_pressure_advance_overhangs: Also adjusts pressure advance on overhangs. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.enable_pressure_advance: Writes this filament's pressure advance value into the G-code, overriding the printer's own or its auto calibration.
notes.filament_adaptive_volumetric_speed: Limits flow by a value fitted from line width and layer height as well as the max volumetric speed. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_flow_ratio: Scales all the plastic pushed for this filament. Calibrate it per spool when tops look rough or gappy; 0.95 to 1.05 is the usual range.
notes.filament_max_volumetric_speed: The most plastic the hotend can melt per second for this filament, in mm3/s. Every speed is capped to stay under it, so it often sets how fast a print really goes.
notes.filament_shrink: How much this filament shrinks in X and Y as it cools, in percent; 99 means a 100 mm part measures 99 mm. The part is scaled up to make up for it.
notes.filament_shrinkage_compensation_z: How much this filament shrinks in height as it cools, in percent. The part is scaled in Z to make up for it.
notes.pellet_flow_coefficient: Converts pellet flow to an equivalent filament diameter on pellet printers. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.pressure_advance: How far ahead the extruder adjusts pressure for speed changes (Klipper's pressure advance, Marlin's linear advance). A calibrated value gives sharp corners without bulges or gaps.
notes.volumetric_speed_coefficients: Coefficients for the fitted flow limit. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.default_filament_colour: The color shown for this filament in the app when no other color is set.
notes.filament_adhesiveness_category: Groups filaments by how well they bond to each other. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_cost: Price per kilogram, used only to estimate the cost of a print.
notes.filament_density: Density of the filament, in g/cm3, used to turn length into weight for estimates. PLA is about 1.24.
notes.filament_diameter: The filament's diameter, in mm, used to work out how far to push it. Must match the spool, usually 1.75 mm.
notes.filament_is_support: Marks the filament as a support material. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_printable: Which kinds of extruder can print this filament. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_soluble: Marks the filament as soluble, such as PVA. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_type: The material, such as PLA, PETG or ABS. It sets safe defaults and checks, such as which plates and temperatures suit the filament.
notes.required_nozzle_HRC: The nozzle hardness this filament needs, on the Rockwell C scale. Abrasive filaments such as carbon fiber blends need a hardened nozzle; 0 means any nozzle.
notes.filament_change_extrusion_role_gcode: G-code for this filament, written each time the print moves to another feature, after the printer's own.
notes.filament_end_gcode: G-code run each time this filament finishes printing, such as before a filament change.
notes.filament_start_gcode: G-code run each time this filament starts printing, such as after a filament change.
notes.filament_change_length: How much filament is pushed through to clear the old one on a filament change, in mm.
notes.filament_change_length_nc: How much filament is pushed through on a nozzle change, in mm, on printers that swap nozzles.
notes.filament_flush_volumetric_speed: Flow while purging this filament, in mm3/s. 0 uses the max volumetric speed.
notes.filament_loading_speed: Speed for loading filament at the prime tower, in mm/s. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_loading_speed_start: Speed at the very start of loading, in mm/s. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_minimal_purge_on_wipe_tower: The least plastic purged into the prime tower after a tool change, in mm3, before purging into infill or an object. It steadies the flow of the new filament.
notes.filament_multitool_ramming: Quickly pushes a little filament into the prime tower just before a tool change on multi-tool printers, which shapes the tip for a clean unload.
notes.filament_multitool_ramming_flow: Flow while ramming before a tool change, in mm3/s.
notes.filament_multitool_ramming_volume: How much filament is rammed before a tool change, in mm3.
notes.filament_prime_volume: How much of this filament is primed into the prime tower after a change, in mm3.
notes.filament_prime_volume_nc: How much filament is primed after a nozzle change, in mm3, on printers that swap nozzles.
notes.filament_ramming_parameters: The ramming speeds the ramming dialog edits. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_ramming_travel_time: Time the nozzle travels while ramming, in seconds. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_ramming_travel_time_nc: Ramming travel time on a nozzle change, in seconds. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_ramming_volumetric_speed: Flow while ramming, in mm3/s; -1 picks it from the filament.
notes.filament_ramming_volumetric_speed_nc: Flow while ramming on a nozzle change, in mm3/s. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_stamping_distance: Pushes the filament toward the nozzle between cooling moves by this much. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_stamping_loading_speed: Speed of the stamping moves. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_toolchange_delay: Waits after unloading, which helps flexible filaments shrink back before the next load. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_d: Pre-extrusion distance where two materials meet in the prime tower, in mm. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_tower_interface_pre_extrusion_l: Pre-extrusion length where two materials meet in the prime tower, in mm. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_tower_interface_purge_volume: Purge length where two materials meet in the prime tower. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_tower_ironing_area: Ironing area where two materials meet in the prime tower. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_unloading_speed: Speed for unloading filament at the prime tower, in mm/s. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_unloading_speed_start: Speed for unloading the filament tip right after ramming, in mm/s. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_notes: Your own notes about this filament.
notes.filament_vendor: Who makes the filament. Shown in the app only.
notes.filament_ironing_flow: Ironing flow for this filament, in percent, over the process value. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_ironing_inset: Ironing inset for this filament, in mm, over the process value. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_ironing_spacing: Ironing line spacing for this filament, in mm, over the process value. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_deretraction_speed: Overrides the printer's deretraction speed for this filament, in mm/s. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_long_retractions_when_cut: Overrides the printer's long retraction before the filament is cut, for this filament. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_retract_after_wipe: How much of the retraction happens after the wipe, in percent. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_retract_before_wipe: Overrides the printer's share of retraction done before the wipe, for this filament. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_retract_length_nc: Retraction before a nozzle change, in mm. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_retract_length_toolchange: Extra retraction before a tool change, in mm. SlicerX does not add it yet; the printer's tool change G-code handles the retraction.
notes.filament_retract_lift_above: Overrides the printer's height above which z hop is used, for this filament. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_retract_lift_below: Overrides the printer's height below which z hop is used, for this filament. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_retract_lift_enforce: Overrides on which surfaces the printer's z hop is used, for this filament. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_retract_restart_extra: Overrides the printer's extra plastic pushed after a retraction, for this filament, in mm. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_retract_restart_extra_toolchang: Extra plastic pushed after a tool change, in mm. SlicerX does not add it yet.
notes.filament_retract_when_changing_layer: Overrides the printer's retraction at each layer change, for this filament. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_retraction_distances_when_cut: Overrides the printer's retraction before the filament is cut, for this filament, in mm. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_retraction_length: Overrides the printer's retraction length for this filament, in mm. Stringy materials such as PETG often want a little more; empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_retraction_minimum_travel: Overrides the printer's shortest travel that triggers a retraction, for this filament. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_retraction_speed: Overrides the printer's retraction speed for this filament, in mm/s. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_wipe: Overrides whether the printer wipes while retracting, for this filament. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_wipe_distance: Overrides the printer's wipe distance for this filament, in mm. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_z_hop: Overrides the printer's z hop height for this filament, in mm. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.filament_z_hop_types: Overrides the printer's z hop type for this filament. Empty uses the printer's value.
notes.long_retractions_when_ec: Does a long retraction when switching extruders, on printers with two nozzles, which reduces oozing from the idle one.
notes.retraction_distances_when_ec: How far to retract when switching extruders, in mm, on printers with two nozzles.
notes.filament_ironing_speed: Ironing speed for this filament, in mm/s, over the process value. Empty uses the process value.
notes.activate_chamber_temp_control: Heats the chamber to the chamber temperature before the print starts and turns it off at the end. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.chamber_minimal_temperature: The chamber temperature at which printing may start while the chamber keeps heating. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.chamber_temperature: Target chamber temperature, in degrees C, for printers with a heated chamber. Helps ABS, ASA, PC and nylon stop warping; keep it low or off for PLA and PETG.
notes.cool_plate_temp: Bed temperature on the Cool Plate after the first layer, in degrees C. 0 means this filament shouldn't print on that plate.
notes.cool_plate_temp_initial_layer: Bed temperature on the Cool Plate for the first layer, in degrees C. 0 means this filament shouldn't print on that plate.
notes.eng_plate_temp: Bed temperature on the Engineering Plate after the first layer, in degrees C. 0 means this filament shouldn't print on that plate.
notes.eng_plate_temp_initial_layer: Bed temperature on the Engineering Plate for the first layer, in degrees C. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_flush_temp: Nozzle temperature while purging this filament, in degrees C. 0 uses the top of its temperature range.
notes.filament_flush_temp_fast: Nozzle temperature for fast purging, in degrees C. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_pre_cooling_temperature: Temperature the nozzle cools to before a filament change, in degrees C. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_pre_cooling_temperature_nc: Temperature the nozzle cools to before a nozzle change, in degrees C. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_preheat_temperature_delta: How far below print temperature the next tool preheats, in degrees C. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.filament_tower_interface_print_temp: Nozzle temperature where two materials meet in the prime tower, in degrees C. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.hot_plate_temp: Bed temperature on the High Temp plate or smooth PEI after the first layer, in degrees C. 0 means this filament shouldn't print on that plate.
notes.hot_plate_temp_initial_layer: Bed temperature on the High Temp plate or smooth PEI for the first layer, in degrees C. 0 means this filament shouldn't print on that plate.
notes.idle_temperature: Nozzle temperature for a tool that isn't printing, in degrees C, when ooze prevention is on. 0 uses the standby temperature delta instead.
notes.nozzle_temperature: Nozzle temperature after the first layer, in degrees C. Hotter flows better and bonds layers more strongly but strings more; stay inside the filament's range.
notes.nozzle_temperature_initial_layer: Nozzle temperature for the first layer, in degrees C. A few degrees hotter than normal helps the first layer stick.
notes.nozzle_temperature_range_high: The hottest nozzle temperature this filament is rated for, in degrees C. SlicerX warns when a setting goes above it.
notes.nozzle_temperature_range_low: The coolest nozzle temperature this filament prints at, in degrees C. SlicerX warns when a setting goes below it.
notes.supertack_plate_temp: Bed temperature on the SuperTack plate after the first layer, in degrees C. 0 means this filament shouldn't print on that plate.
notes.supertack_plate_temp_initial_layer: Bed temperature on the SuperTack plate for the first layer, in degrees C. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.temperature_vitrification: The temperature where this filament softens, in degrees C. With the bed this hot or hotter, open the door or lid so the filament path doesn't clog.
notes.textured_cool_plate_temp: Bed temperature on the Textured Cool Plate after the first layer, in degrees C. 0 means this filament shouldn't print on that plate.
notes.textured_cool_plate_temp_initial_layer: Bed temperature on the Textured Cool Plate for the first layer, in degrees C. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.textured_plate_temp: Bed temperature on textured PEI after the first layer, in degrees C. 0 means this filament shouldn't print on that plate.
notes.textured_plate_temp_initial_layer: Bed temperature on textured PEI for the first layer, in degrees C. 0 means this filament shouldn't print on that plate.
notes.auxiliary_fan: Tells SlicerX the printer has an auxiliary part cooling fan, driven with M106 P2. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.cooling_filter_enabled: Marks that the printer's cooling filter is fitted. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.enable_pre_heating: Preheats the next tool before a tool change. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.fan_kickstart: Runs the fan at full speed for this many seconds before dropping to the target, for fans that don't start at low power. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.fan_speedup_overhangs: Applies the fan speedup time only to overhangs. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.fan_speedup_time: Starts the fan this many seconds early so it is at speed when needed. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.part_cooling_fan_min_pwm: Raises any fan command above zero to at least this percent, for fans that won't spin at low power. 0 leaves fan commands as they are.
notes.support_chamber_temp_control: Tells SlicerX the printer can heat and control its chamber temperature.
notes.support_cooling_filter: Tells SlicerX the printer can take a cooling filter. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.support_multi_bed_types: Lets the printer use several kinds of bed plate. SlicerX keeps this for profile exchange and does not use it yet.
notes.before_layer_change_gcode: G-code run at every layer change, before the nozzle moves up.
